citations.text:
Study Endpoints

Mean change from baseline in mean diurnal IOP (defined as the mean of the four diurnal time points: 09:00, 12:00, 15:00, 18:00 h) at day 8/day 9;

The primary efficacy endpoint was mean change from baseline in mean nocturnal IOP (defined as the mean of the four nocturnal time points: 21:00, 00:00, 03:00, and 06:00 h) at day 8/day 9. The secondary efficacy endpoints as prespecified in the statistical analysis plan were:

The mean change from baseline in mean nocturnal IOP within each treatment group was tested using one-sample t tests and 90% t-distribution confidence intervals around the mean change. Two-sample t tests and 90% t-distribution confidence intervals around the difference in the mean nocturnal IOP between the two treatments (netarsudil—vehicle) were employed, using the Satterthwaite approximation for unequal variance, as the primary statistical comparisons between netarsudil and vehicle.

5.1.reasoning: The paper lists mean diurnal IOP change as a pre‑specified endpoint and refers to a statistical analysis plan that defined secondary endpoints, indicating the analysis was planned, but the timing of the plan relative to data collection is not documented.
